strong_findings.summary: Extends Vento's two-photon QED (arXiv:2507.06697, on the known list as C4 partial) to the electroweak theory: the ordinary photon couples only to electric charges, an 'extraordinary' photon only to magnetic ones, and the new photon and the monopoles form the dark matter sector, joined to ours by kinetic mixing.
strong_findings.difference: Dark matter made of magnetic charges under their own photon, the shape of C4's separate-photon form, but with no position/momentum polarization; one magnetic species against the electron, not an analog for each charged particle; couplings tied by the Schwinger condition with mixing, not fixed by reciprocity as an S-image. Same label as the earlier Vento paper, for consistency.

strong_findings.citation: J. Govaerts, 'Magnetic monopoles with no strings attached: a portal to the dark side of dual electrodynamics', Eur. Phys. J. C 83 (2023) 158, arXiv:2302.03526.
strong_findings.summary: In SO(2)-dual electrodynamics written with doubled potentials, an action principle for point charges gives a generalised Lorentz force. Under it, electrically and magnetically charged matter are electromagnetically 'dark' to each other except through one new coupling. The conclusions ask whether this gives a dark-matter candidate: 'a dark parallel world of purely magnetically charged matter' that interacts 'ever so weakly' with 'the purely electrically charged matter of our visible Universe' while contributing to the energy-momentum tensor. As a question, this states the magnetic half of (dual) electromagnetism as a dark, gravitating mirror of our electric matter: the core of C4's shared-photon form.
strong_findings.difference: There is no position-momentum structure: the magnetic world is dark because of the form of the action-derived Lorentz force, not because it is localized in momentum. There is no Born reciprocity, no polarization, and no claim that each electrically charged particle has a magnetic analog. It is posed as a question, with no model of the magnetic matter's spectrum, abundance or Parker-bound status. The darkness rests on a Lorentz force that departs from the usual dual-invariant one. Citing papers (7) do not develop the dark-matter question beyond Vento 2025 (next entry).

strong_findings.summary: A two-photon (Cabibbo-Ferrari type) QED: the ordinary photon couples only to electric charge and an 'extraordinary' photon only to magnetic charge. The monopole and the extraordinary photon form the dark sector, with the monopoles taken to be the dark matter; the electron and the ordinary photon form the visible sector. Kinetic mixing turns electrons and monopoles into dyons, and a Schwinger condition ties the dark magnetic coupling g to e. The model is offered against the background of the monopole null result. This is C4's separate-photon form (magnetic analogs under their own photon, with a coupling Dirac-tied to ours) without the momentum polarization.
strong_findings.difference: There is no position-momentum or reciprocity structure: the dark sector is an ordinary position-space sector. Ordinary matter is simplified to electrons and dark matter to one monopole species, not a full mirror family. The portal is kinetic mixing, which the program's strict P4 excludes. Nothing selects the electric frame by a vacuum event. Preprint only.

strong_findings.citation: F. C. Adams, M. Fatuzzo, K. Freese, G. Tarle, R. Watkins, M. S. Turner, 'Extension of the Parker bound on the flux of magnetic monopoles', Phys. Rev. Lett. 70 (1993) 2511.
strong_findings.summary: Survival and growth of a small galactic seed field bounds the flux of monopoles of our photon by 10^-16 (m/10^17 GeV) cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1. This 'rules out the possibility that monopoles much lighter than 10^17 GeV/c^2 can provide the closure density'. It weighs against the shared-photon form if the analogs are localized in position and make up a large share of the dark matter.
strong_findings.difference: It applies to ordinary, position-localized monopoles moving through galactic fields. #11 §11.4 already states the conflict (through #14's Parker comparison, not gated) and asks for p-localization or binding to hide the analogs. The bound says nothing about objects whose field profile is spread in position. Screening (Carneiro 2026, below) is a published third way such bounds are evaded.

related.summary: S-duality of four-dimensional gauge theories is formulated as a canonical transformation in the phase space of the theory, giving tau~ = -1/tau. Electric-magnetic duality is a phase-space (conjugate-variable) transformation, as Born's rho is.

not_found_statements.statement: A matter sector related to ours by a position-momentum exchange (Born reciprocity, Fourier transform, T-duality, dual spacetime, phase-space polarization), whose particles are the magnetically charged counterparts of our electrically charged particles: the magnetic mirror as stated in #11 §11.4.

Shared-photon form: magnetic charges of our own photon carried by matter localized in momentum (in the field profile), so that the magnetic half of electromagnetism lives in the conjugate polarization and is hidden from position-space searches and the Parker bound.
One vacuum event (one order parameter) selecting both the position polarization of phase space and the electric sublattice of the charge lattice (#11 §11.3-§11.4, the electric-sublattice clause).
A conjugate or dark sector whose gauge coupling is fixed at the S-dual of ours (alpha_d = 1/(4 alpha) or 1/alpha) by a reciprocity map.
Born's own reciprocity papers relating reciprocity to magnetic charge or to an electric-magnetic exchange.

No work places a magnetically charged counterpart of every electrically charged particle in a dual, conjugate, reciprocal or momentum-space sector. Full magnetic counterpart families appear only in ordinary space (Sullivan-Fryberger 2015, Fryberger 2018, Polchinski's completeness, Krasnoholovets 2019); a dark sector of magnetic charges under its own photon appears without any position-momentum structure (García-Moreno-Vento 2026, after Vento 2025); and works joining Born reciprocity, Fourier or T-duality to electric-magnetic duality do so formally, inside one theory (Jafarizadeh-Rezaei-Aghdam 1999, De Haro-Cinti 2025, Kriger 2026, the last excluding monopoles). No work combines S-duality and Born's rho to put the magnetic half of electromagnetism in the p-polarization (the shared-photon form).

No lineage paper pairs each electrically charged position-polarized particle with a magnetically charged momentum-polarized analog, or ties S-duality to Born's rotation. Born's school wrote a 'Reciprocity theory of electrodynamics' (Born, Cheng, Green, Nature 164, 281 (1949)); only its first paragraph was reachable, and it concerns divergences.

Statement 1 (a matter sector related to ours by a position-momentum exchange whose particles are the magnetic counterparts of our electric ones). Holds. None of my 31 lit.py queries, 3 WebSearch queries or citation sweeps found it, and on reading, the searcher's closest paper does not state it either: in Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2021 the dark x~-dependent fields carry the same algebras as the visible ones, and the Langlands (e-m) duality relates the two heterotic E8 factors. The closest papers are now Govaerts 2023 (a question; shared-photon-like) and Vento 2025 (a model; separate-photon-like), neither with position-momentum structure, and at the level of mechanism Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2021 and Gibbons-Herdeiro 2000.

Statement 2 (shared-photon form with the magnetic charges of our photon hidden by localization in momentum). Holds. INSPIRE full text for monopoles plus momentum space plus dark matter plus position space (16 hits), Born reciprocity plus dark matter plus magnetic charge (1), T-dual plus winding plus dark matter plus magnetic charge (4 theses), and two extended WebSearch queries returned nothing on it. The published hiding mechanisms remain screening (Carneiro 2026), the force law of a doubled-potential theory (Govaerts 2023), confinement under mixing (Terning-Verhaaren; Graesser et al.) and winding-space localization of a KK monopole (Harvey-Jensen 2005, not our photon).

Statement 3 (one vacuum event selecting both the position polarization and the electric sublattice). Holds. INSPIRE abstracts joining spontaneous breaking of e-m duality to position, phase space, momentum space or reciprocity: 0 hits; without that restriction, 17 hits, none of which ties a duality-frame choice to a phase-space polarization (by title: Chan and Tsou on Yang-Mills duality as the origin of fermion generations, supersymmetric gauge dynamics, lattice and condensed-matter symmetry breaking). Carneiro 2026 remains nearest: a vacuum selects the electric frame only.

Statement 4 (a conjugate or dark sector whose coupling is fixed at the S-dual of ours by a reciprocity map). Holds. Full-text searches for a dark fine-structure constant with S-duality or Dirac quantization returned 0, 0 and 1 hit (Graesser et al., already listed). The only precedent found for reciprocity fixing a coupling is Born 1940 on Landé's argument that reciprocity gives 137, which concerns our own alpha (new finding, abstract only).

Statement 5 (Born's own reciprocity papers relating reciprocity to magnetic charge). Holds on the evidence available, with a caveat. INSPIRE lists 11 of Born's reciprocity papers (1938-1950); no title mentions magnetic poles. The searcher read Born 1949 (Rev. Mod. Phys.). The abstracts of Born, Cheng and Green 1949, 'Reciprocity Theory of Electrodynamics' (Nature 164, 281), and of Born 1940 on the number 137 contain nothing magnetic. The full texts of Born 1938 (Royal Society: HTTP 403 again; no free copy found by WebSearch), Born 1940 (Cambridge Core, no access) and Born-Cheng-Green 1949 (Nature login) were not read, so for those three the statement rests on abstracts.
